metadata.name: Paul's 3rd Missionary Journey
metadata.description: Paul's extended ministry in Ephesus and return to Jerusalem (~53-57 AD)

properties.name: Antioch (Syria)
properties.description: After spending some time in Antioch, Paul set out and traveled systematically through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

properties.name: Ephesus
properties.description: Paul spent three years in Ephesus — the longest stay anywhere in his journeys. He reasoned daily in the hall of Tyrannus. Extraordinary miracles occurred; many who practiced magic burned their scrolls (worth 50,000 drachmas). The riot of Demetrius the silversmith erupted over Diana (Artemis) of the Ephesians.

properties.name: Macedonia (Philippi)
properties.description: Paul traveled through Macedonia, speaking many words of encouragement to the believers. He spent three months in Greece before returning through Macedonia.

properties.name: Corinth (Greece)
properties.description: Paul spent three months in Greece (Corinth). When a plot against him was discovered, he changed his plan to sail directly to Syria and went back through Macedonia.

properties.name: Philippi
properties.description: At Troas, a young man named Eutychus fell asleep during Paul's late-night sermon and fell from a third-floor window. Paul embraced him and he was restored to life.

properties.name: Miletus
properties.description: Paul summoned the Ephesian elders to Miletus. He warned of wolves entering the flock and committed them to God. They wept as he knelt and prayed, grieving that they would see his face no more.

properties.name: Tyre
properties.event_name: Disciples Urge Paul Not to Go
properties.description: Through the Spirit, disciples at Tyre urged Paul not to go on to Jerusalem. After seven days they knelt on the beach, prayed together, and said farewell.

properties.name: Caesarea Maritima
properties.description: Philip the evangelist hosted Paul. The prophet Agabus bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt and said: The Holy Spirit says that in this way the Jews in Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.

properties.name: Jerusalem
properties.description: The brothers in Jerusalem welcomed Paul warmly. He reported in detail what God had done among the Gentiles, and they praised God. The journey that led to his arrest had begun.
